description: Flames rip from the earth's surface, spewing 40+ feet into the nights sky. Residents look on in awe as yet another fossil fuel pipeline has exploded. An all to common scene throughout rural America these days.  Many all around the world have already taken to boycott and direct action to attempt to bring some of these  oil giants to their knees. With increased action every day its only a matter of time before they can no longer sustain the extraction.

faqs.answer: A pipeline owned by Mid-America Pipeline Co LLC (a shell company of Louisiana-based Enterprise Products Partners) exploded near Smithville, MO on November 29, 2016, carrying liquid propane and ethane gas. Flames were visible from I-29 and Kansas City International Airport.
faqs.question: What pipeline exploded near Kansas City in November 2016?

faqs.answer: No injuries or major environmental damage were reported, as the explosion occurred roughly a half mile from the nearest home. Crews shut off valves to stop gas flow and the blaze burned itself out.
faqs.question: Were there any injuries from the Smithville pipeline explosion?

faqs.answer: The EPA documented 6,763 pipeline spills in just four years, causing $7 billion in damages, demonstrating that fossil fuel pipeline infrastructure carries significant and recurring risks to communities and the environment.
faqs.question: How many pipeline spills has the EPA documented?

faqs.answer: Activists worldwide have engaged in boycotts, direct action blockades, legal challenges, and divestment campaigns against oil giants. The Standing Rock resistance and other pipeline protests represent a growing movement against fossil fuel extraction.
faqs.question: What direct actions have people taken against fossil fuel pipelines?

leadParagraph: Another Day Another Pipeline Explosion in America. Leaves Many Asking When is Enough, Enough?
methodology: This article was originally published on the Anon Resistance News website (anonresistance.news) and has been migrated to UnTelevised Media.
title: As Yet Another Pipeline Explodes, We Must Ask When is Enough, Enough?
